title: Long PLTR — Defense-AI Demand Zone Re-entry; SpaceX Federal Data Infrastructure Catalyst
entry: Initiate $138–143 (the demand zone explicitly defined in the June 5 briefing; scale in on any NFP-driven intraday weakness). 70% at open on any print in zone; 30% add at $138–139.50 if initial volatility pushes lower. Do not chase above $145 on the open regardless of NFP outcome.
stop_loss: $131.00 daily close (~6.8% below entry midpoint $140.50) — implies demand zone has structurally failed and PLTR is reverting to pre-Iran-premium base levels, OR a broader risk-off event (NFP bear case + VIX above 20) forces de-grossing across high-multiple government-AI names.

$170 — FY2026 revenue guidance raised again above $3.80B on accelerating US commercial and government segments; PLTR added to S&P 500 if not already included; +21.0%

catalyst: PLTR pulled back from its June 4 close of $143.50 (+9.5% that session) to the $140–142 demand zone in early June 5 trading. The morning briefing explicitly defines $138–142 as the demand zone and 'do not chase above $150.' The prior PLTR opportunity (long-pltr-government-ai-iran-geopolitical-2026-05-28) hit Target 1 at $156.54 (+18.1%) and is closed — this is a fresh entry at the pullback demand zone. Incremental catalyst: SpaceX IPO roadshow opens June 8 at $135/share ($1.77T valuation), targeting $75B raise. Palantir is the primary AI-enabled federal data analytics platform for Space Force, SPACECOM, and DOD programs that will need to manage the SpaceX government contract data ecosystem at scale.
thesis:
Palantir pulled back from $143.50 (June 4 close) to the $140–142 demand zone in the first hour of June 5 trading — a healthy consolidation after a 9.5% single-session gain. The morning briefing explicitly defines this zone as the re-entry level and warns against chasing above $150. This opportunity captures the fresh entry at technical support with an incrementally stronger fundamental thesis than the prior PLTR position that hit Target 1 at $156.54.

The SpaceX SPCX IPO — roadshow opening June 8, pricing June 11, trading June 12 — is the single most significant new catalyst for Palantir's government contract pipeline. At $75B raised and $1.77T valuation, SpaceX will be the largest company ever to go public in the U.S. government-commercial space. SpaceX's operations — Starlink satellite telemetry, Falcon launch manifests, Starship test data, and the USSF and NASA contract data streams — generate enormous sovereign data flows that require Top Secret/SCI-certified AI analytics at scale. Palantir's Foundry and AIP platforms are the only commercially available AI data infrastructure products with the relevant government certifications and operational track record. As SpaceX moves from private to public, its institutional partners in the federal government will accelerate investment in the data infrastructure needed to manage the newly public company's government-commercial data pipeline. Palantir is the natural beneficiary.

The underlying fundamentals have not changed. PLTR Q1 FY2026 revenue grew 39% year-over-year; US commercial revenue grew 71% YoY; US government revenue grew 45% YoY. The company raised FY2026 full-year guidance to $3.75–3.80B with a Rule of 40 score above 80. Adjusted operating margins of 51% make PLTR the highest-margin defense-AI platform available to investors. The government-AI thesis that drove the prior long from $130 to $156 — federal AI budgets expanding, Iran geopolitical threat increasing demand for ISR and AI-enabled targeting — remains structurally intact. The pullback to $140–142 is profit-taking after a sharp move, not fundamental deterioration.

The stop at $131 is 6.6% below the entry midpoint and represents the structural support zone established before the May 2026 Iran escalation began adding a geopolitical premium to defense-AI names. A close below $131 would imply the demand zone has failed and the stock is reverting to base levels — at that point, the SpaceX catalyst read would need reassessment. The risk-reward at 3.6:1 to the third target reflects the combination of a high-conviction re-entry at a well-defined demand zone and a structural catalyst (SpaceX IPO) with a specific timeline.
bull_case: SpaceX SPCX IPO generates $75B in capital allocation and immediately triggers DOD/USSF announcements about expanded SpaceX-Palantir data infrastructure partnerships. PLTR Q2 FY2026 earnings (early August) beat on both revenue and guidance; US commercial ACV accelerates above 80% YoY. Stock re-rates toward $170 on the combination of SpaceX federal catalyst + earnings beat. If Anthropic and OpenAI IPO timelines are confirmed (targeting September 2026 per search results), the government-AI data infrastructure spend would expand further, taking PLTR toward $190.
bear_case: NFP fires the bear case (hot print + 30Y above 5.00%), triggering a broad risk-off de-grossing that pressures high-multiple growth names regardless of fundamentals. PLTR falls through $131 support. Alternatively, SpaceX federal contract integration is slower than expected — SpaceX keeps its data operations internal rather than licensing Palantir's platform. US government AI spending faces Congressional scrutiny or a continuing resolution that slows discretionary AI contract awards.
invalidation: $131.00 daily close, OR PLTR reports Q2 FY2026 revenue below $870M (below FY guidance run-rate) and cuts guidance, OR SpaceX announces a competing in-house AI data infrastructure platform that directly displaces PLTR from the federal space-data ecosystem.
